title: Automorphisms of domain products and stabilizer fixed rings
statement: Let $I$ be a finite set and let $B_i$ for $i\in I$ be commutative integral domains, meaning nonzero commutative unital rings without zero divisors. Put $B=\prod_{i\in I}B_i$, and let a group $H$ act on $B$ by unital ring automorphisms $\alpha_h$, with $\alpha_{gh}=\alpha_g\alpha_h$. For $i\in I$, let $e_i\in B$ be the coordinate idempotent ($e_i^2=e_i$, the convention in [lem-weil-pbc-spec-clopen-idempotent]) with coordinate $1$ at $i$ and $0$ elsewhere. There is a unique action of $H$ on $I$ satisfying $\alpha_h(e_i)=e_{hi}$. There are unique ring isomorphisms $h_i:B_i\xrightarrow{\sim}B_{hi}$ satisfying $(\alpha_h(x))_{hi}=h_i(x_i)$ for all $x\in B$; these satisfy $(gh)_i=g_{hi}\circ h_i$. Choose a subset $R\subseteq I$ containing one representative of every orbit. Write $H_i=\{h\in H:hi=i\}$, $C_i=\{c\in B_i:h_i(c)=c\text{ for all }h\in H_i\}$, and $B^H=\{x\in B:\alpha_h(x)=x\text{ for all }h\in H\}$, with their inherited ring structures. Projection to the representative coordinates is a ring isomorphism $B^H\xrightarrow{\sim}\prod_{i\in R}C_i$. Its inverse sends $(c_i)_{i\in R}$ to the tuple specified by $x_{hi}=h_i(c_i)$. These assertions include $I=\varnothing$, when both product rings are the zero ring; no faithfulness or finiteness of $H$ is required.

source.place: Tag 00EE, lemma-disjoint-decomposition, for the idempotent context; the stated group-action and varying-factor fixed-ring comparison is agent-formulated from the component/stabilizer calculation of ILO X 2.3 Step 3, printed pp.151--152, and retained item proof steps 4--5. Tag 00EE alone does not assert this comparison.

proof.text: If $I=\varnothing$, then $R=\varnothing$ and $B$ has one element. Every action on it and on the empty set is unique, the factor assertions have no instances, and projection is the unique isomorphism between the two one-element rings. Hence assume $I\ne\varnothing$ below.

source.place: Agent coordinate proof of the component/stabilizer calculation: ILO X 2.3 Step 3, printed pp.151--152 (PDF pp.157--158); Stacks Tag 00EE (lemma-disjoint-decomposition) supplies only the idempotent convention, not this theorem. Coordinate argument, step 1.

proof.text: An idempotent $u\in B$ has $u_j(u_j-1)=0$ in each domain $B_j$, so every $u_j$ is $0$ or $1$. For idempotents define $v\le u$ to mean $vu=v$. Coordinatewise, this says that every coordinate where $v$ is $1$ is also a coordinate where $u$ is $1$. Thus the minimal nonzero idempotents are exactly the $e_i$: each singleton support is minimal, while any nonzero $u$ has a coordinate $i$ equal to $1$, and then $0\ne e_i\le u$; minimality forces $u=e_i$. Distinct indices give distinct $e_i$, since $0\ne1$ in each $B_i$.

source.place: Agent coordinate proof of the component/stabilizer calculation: ILO X 2.3 Step 3, printed pp.151--152 (PDF pp.157--158); Stacks Tag 00EE (lemma-disjoint-decomposition) supplies only the idempotent convention, not this theorem. Coordinate argument, step 2.

proof.text: A ring automorphism preserves idempotency, nonzeroness and the relation $vu=v$, in both directions by applying its inverse. It therefore permutes the minimal nonzero idempotents of step 2. Define $hi$ by the unique equality $\alpha_h(e_i)=e_{hi}$. The inverse permutation is the one for $h^{-1}$. Since $\alpha_1=\mathrm{id}$ and $\alpha_{gh}=\alpha_g\alpha_h$, these equalities give $1i=i$ and $(gh)i=g(hi)$. They also prove uniqueness of the action.

source.place: Agent coordinate proof of the component/stabilizer calculation: ILO X 2.3 Step 3, printed pp.151--152 (PDF pp.157--158); Stacks Tag 00EE (lemma-disjoint-decomposition) supplies only the idempotent convention, not this theorem. Coordinate argument, step 3.

proof.text: For $a\in B_i$ let $\delta_i(a)$ be the tuple supported at $i$ with value $a$, and define $h_i(a)=(\alpha_h(\delta_i(a)))_{hi}$. The identities $e_i\delta_i(a)=\delta_i(a)$ and $\alpha_h(e_i)=e_{hi}$ show that $\alpha_h(\delta_i(a))=\delta_{hi}(h_i(a))$. Additivity and multiplicativity follow by applying $\alpha_h$ and evaluation to the corresponding identities for $\delta_i$; also $h_i(1)=1$ because $\delta_i(1)=e_i$. Applying $\alpha_{h^{-1}}$ proves that $(h^{-1})_{hi}$ is its inverse. For arbitrary $x$, use $e_ix=\delta_i(x_i)$ and apply $\alpha_h$ to obtain $(\alpha_h(x))_{hi}=h_i(x_i)$. This formula on $x=\delta_i(a)$ proves uniqueness. Applying $\alpha_g\alpha_h$ to $\delta_i(a)$ gives $(gh)_i(a)=g_{hi}(h_i(a))$; similarly $1_i=\mathrm{id}$.

source.place: Agent coordinate proof of the component/stabilizer calculation: ILO X 2.3 Step 3, printed pp.151--152 (PDF pp.157--158); Stacks Tag 00EE (lemma-disjoint-decomposition) supplies only the idempotent convention, not this theorem. Coordinate argument, step 4.

proof.text: For $h\in H_i$ the maps $h_i$ are automorphisms of $B_i$ and satisfy the action laws by step 4. Their common fixed elements form a subring: every such map preserves $0,1$, sums, products and negatives, so these operations preserve the fixed-element equations. The same observation gives the subring $B^H$. If $x\in B^H$ and $h\in H_i$, the coordinate formula gives $h_i(x_i)=x_i$. Thus evaluation defines a unital ring homomorphism $E:B^H\to\prod_{i\in R}C_i$, using coordinatewise operations.

source.place: Agent coordinate proof of the component/stabilizer calculation: ILO X 2.3 Step 3, printed pp.151--152 (PDF pp.157--158); Stacks Tag 00EE (lemma-disjoint-decomposition) supplies only the idempotent convention, not this theorem. Coordinate argument, step 5.

proof.text: Given $c=(c_i)_{i\in R}$, define $x_j=h_i(c_i)$ whenever $j=hi$ with $i\in R$. Such $i,h$ exist by the representative property. The representative $i$ is unique. If $hi=h'i$, put $k=h^{-1}h'\in H_i$, so $h'=hk$. Then step 4 gives $h'_i(c_i)=h_{ki}(k_i(c_i))=h_i(c_i)$, since $ki=i$ and $c_i\in C_i$. This proves independence of every choice and defines the tuple $x$.

source.place: Agent coordinate proof of the component/stabilizer calculation: ILO X 2.3 Step 3, printed pp.151--152 (PDF pp.157--158); Stacks Tag 00EE (lemma-disjoint-decomposition) supplies only the idempotent convention, not this theorem. Coordinate argument, step 6.

proof.text: For $g\in H$ and $j=hi$ as in step 6, the coordinate formula and the cocycle identity give $(\alpha_g(x))_{gj}=g_j(x_j)=g_{hi}(h_i(c_i))=(gh)_i(c_i)=x_{gj}$. The permutation $j\mapsto gj$ is surjective, hence $\alpha_g(x)=x$. Thus extension gives a map $T:\prod_{i\in R}C_i\to B^H$.

source.place: Agent coordinate proof of the component/stabilizer calculation: ILO X 2.3 Step 3, printed pp.151--152 (PDF pp.157--158); Stacks Tag 00EE (lemma-disjoint-decomposition) supplies only the idempotent convention, not this theorem. Coordinate argument, step 7.

proof.text: Taking $h=1$ at a representative gives $(E(T(c)))_i=1_i(c_i)=c_i$. Conversely, if $x\in B^H$ and $j=hi$ with $i\in R$, then $(T(E(x)))_j=h_i(x_i)=(\alpha_h(x))_{hi}=x_j$. Hence $E$ is bijective with inverse $T$. As $E$ is a unital ring homomorphism, it is the asserted ring isomorphism, with precisely the displayed inverse formula. The proof used neither faithfulness nor finiteness of $H$.

Step 2: idempotents in a product of domains have coordinates 0 or 1, the minimal nonzero idempotents are exactly the e_i, and they are distinct because each factor is nonzero. Step 3: the automorphisms permute the e_i, which gives a unique action. Step 4: h_i(a)=(alpha_h delta_i(a))_{hi} satisfies the support identity, is unital, has inverse (h^{-1})_{hi}, satisfies the coordinate formula and the cocycle identity, and is unique. Finiteness and faithfulness of H are never used. Cases tested: I empty; ZxZ with the swap (diagonal); C with conjugation (fixed ring R); infinite and non-faithful H; characteristic 2.
